author: Chris Stein in Washington
description:
Trump ally, accused of an array of illegal acts, had earlier condemned impeachment push as ‘a farce and a stunt’

House Republicans on Tuesday blocked an effort to impeach Pete Hegseth, rejecting allegations that the defense secretary had repeatedly violated the constitution through his handling of the Iran war and other conflicts globally.

The vote came a week after Republicans lost control of the Senate and House of Representatives in their worst midterm election in more than a half century, and underscored how lawmakers remain wary of crossing Donald Trump, who has signaled his continued support for Hegseth.

Continue reading...
title: House Republicans block effort to impeach Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Progressive senator says ‘I like Chuck … but the time is now for change’ as calls grow for new Democratic leadership

Bernie Sanders, a progressive senator from Vermont, said on Tuesday he would not support Chuck Schumer’s bid to serve as the Democratic leader in the US Senate, joining a growing cohort of Democrats calling for a change in leadership.

“I personally have known Chuck Schumer for over 30 years, and I like Chuck. Nobody who works harder than Chuck Schumer. But in my view, the time is now for change, and I will not be supporting Chuck to be re-elected as the Democratic leader,” Sanders told reporters on Capitol Hill.

Continue reading...</
title: Bernie Sanders says he will not back Schumer for Senate Democratic leader

author: Maya Yang
description:
The federal agency is requiring all GLP-1s to include information about the potential risk on warning labels

The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a new warning on GLP-1 medications – which can facilitate weight loss – over a rare eye condition that could lead to sudden and permanent blindness.

On Monday, the FDA announced that it is requiring all GLP-1 medications – including Novo Nordisk’s Ozempic and Wegovy, Eli Lilly’s Mounjaro and Zepbound, as well as Sanofi’s Soliqua – to include information about the potential risk of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, also known as NAION, on warning labels.

Continue reading...</
title: FDA warns of rare eye condition causing blindness from GLP-1 weight loss medications

author: Sam Levin
description:
Voters adopted extreme policy requiring medical sex verification for all girls who want to play team sports

Parents of student athletes in Washington state have sued to block a ballot initiative banning transgender girls from women’s sports teams, calling the measure discriminatory and warning it would lead to “invasive” genital examinations for female athletes.

Last week, voters in the solidly Democratic state passed Initiative 638, a major setback for LGBTQ+ rights amid the “blue wave” of the US midterm elections. Nebraska, Colorado and Arizona adopted similar anti-trans sports bans, though advocates say Washington state’s policy is particularly extreme due to its medical
title: Parents sue to stop Washington state trans sports ban that could require ‘invasive’ genital exams

author: Guardian staff
description:
As Democrats prepare to take control of Congress, Republicans pick Jordan for last two years of Trump’s presidency

Republican lawmakers have elected Jim Jordan, veteran congressman and Trump loyalist, as their leader in the House of Representatives following resounding losses in last week’s US midterm elections.

As Democrats prepare to take control of both chambers of US Congress in January, Republicans backed Jordan to lead them in the House for the last two years of Donald Trump’s presidency.

Continue reading...
title: Republicans elect Jim Jordan as House minority leader after midterm defeats

author: Jeremy Barr in Washington
description:
Senators pressured Danielle Thumann, senior counsel to FCC chair Brendan Carr, to speak about agency’s actions toward ABC and Jimmy Kimmel

During a contentious Tuesday hearing on her nomination by Donald Trump to serve as a Federal Communications Commission (FCC) commissioner, Senate Democrats hammered Danielle Thumann about recent actions taken by the Brendan Carr-led regulator that have been criticized as hostile to press freedom.

Thumann, who serves as senior counsel to Carr, is expected to be approved as commissioner, with Republicans in charge of the US Senate and House. But Ben Ray Luján, a senator of New Mexico, assured her that the commission’s actions will be under close scrutiny when Democrats take charge of the chamber in January.

Continue reading...
title: Trump’s FCC nominee avoids questions from Democrats on Carr’s ‘censorship agenda’

author: Anna Betts
description:
Republicans on House panel criticize US government’s investigation into Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell

Republicans on the House oversight committee released a report on Tuesday criticizing the federal government’s handling of the investigations into Jeffrey Epstein and his associate, Ghislaine Maxwell, and called on the Department of Justice to interview “key witnesses, investigate Epstein associates accused of criminal activity, and ensure survivors have access to their records”.

“The federal government has failed the survivors of Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell’s horrific crimes for decades,” James Comer, the Republican congressman who chairs the committee, said in a statement.

C
title: House Republicans urge DoJ to further investigate ‘key witnesses’ in Epstein case

author: Haroon Siddique Legal affairs correspondent
description:
Criminal Bar Association and campaigners hail Mr Justice Bennathan for delivering remarks with ‘piercing clarity’

The judge who sentenced Russell Brand has been praised for dispelling rape myths with “piercing clarity”.

Mr Justice Bennathan’s sentencing remarks were particularly welcomed given that rape myths had played a part in the trial. He was also lauded for calling out “enablers” who witnessed sexual assaults by the comedian.

Continue reading...
title: Judge who sentenced Russell Brand praised for dispelling rape myths

author: Steven Morris and Glyn Bellis
description:
Jury finds Blade Silvano, who presented herself as a male army veteran, guilty of six counts of sexual assault

A woman serving a prison sentence for sexual assault after pretending to be a man and duping a woman into a physical relationship has been found guilty of tricking another woman into a similar abusive partnership.

In both cases, Blade Silvano, 44, met the women on an online dating site and falsely claimed she was a man who had served in the armed forces before meeting them in person and sexually assaulting them.

Information and support for anyone affected by rape or sexual abuse issues is available from the following organisations. In the UK, Rape Crisis offers support on 0808 500 2222 in England and Wales, 0808 801 0302 in Scotland, or 0800 0246 991 in Northern Ireland. In the US, R
title: Woman jailed for posing as man to dupe partner into sex found guilty of similar deception

author: Sally Weale and Kiran Stacey
description:
Hamish Falconer says UK has ‘not accepted principle’ of linking electricity trade to ‘cohesion fund’ but two sides will discuss issue

Britain is willing to discuss paying towards infrastructure schemes in poorer parts of the EU in return for access to the European electricity market, according to the minister in charge of renegotiating the bilateral relationship.

Hamish Falconer, the cabinet minister in charge of EU talks, told the Guardian he was sure the two sides would discuss the issue after this month’s summit, as ministers look to deepen ties with the union over the next few years.

Continue reading...
title: Britain willing to discuss paying into EU to join electricity market, says minister

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
Regulations under consideration could affect up to 150 platforms, including LegoPlay, Spotify and eBay, sources say

A substantial expansion of the social media ban for under-16s could inadvertently lead to a ban on YouTube Kids and other sites that had been thought exempt, sources briefed on the government’s proposals have said.

The ban could also see games platforms such as Lego Play covered by the regulations. One source close to the talks said the regulations now under consideration meant there could be up to 150 platforms now covered by the ban, which is set to come into force in March.

Continue reading...
title: UK social media ban expansion for under-16s could cover YouTube Kids

author: Dan Sabbagh in Oslo
description:
New alliance with the Netherlands and Baltic and Nordic countries comes in response to 41% increase in Russian naval activity around UK

Russian naval activity around the UK has increased by 41% in the first nine months of the year, a British defence minister has said, as the Royal Navy announced plans to step up a 10-country maritime defensive effort in response.

Luke Pollard, the minister for defence readiness, described the figure as “a huge increase”, justifying a new drone and warship initiative from “the alliance of beer-drinking nations” – the UK, the Netherlands and the Baltic and Nordic countries.

Continue reading...
title: Russian naval aggression prompts new defensive initiative with ‘beer-drinking nations’

author: Guardian staff
description:
The suspect, tracked down from surveillance video, claims to have had a medical emergency

An apparently sports-mad parent from a Michigan high school has stunned authorities and triggered a police investigation after allegedly entering a rival school and defecating in a corridor.

The bizarre case unfolded at the Grosse Pointe South school with the parent a fan of fierce local rival Bedford high school. The two schools were engaged in a district championship football game on Friday, the Detroit TV news outlet WXYZ reported.
title: Michigan sports parent allegedly defecates in rival high school’s corridor: ‘definitely a first’

author: Tobi Thomas Health and inequalities correspondent
description:
Premature death risk also varies according to employment and qualifications, shows analysis ‘laying bare the scale of inequalities’

People living in the most deprived areas of England are more than twice as likely to die prematurely than their more affluent counterparts, according to analysis.

The research, conducted by the Health Foundation, took demographic data from the 2021 census to look at differences in premature mortality rates – defined as any adult who died before their 75th birthday – alongside further data on deaths from March 2021 to December 2023.

Continue reading...
title: People in deprived areas of England more than twice as likely to die early, study shows

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Juan Vargas, a congressman, says he’s working to reunite the third-grader with loved ones

Relatives of an eight-year-old Haitian boy who was taken into custody by federal immigration authorities in California are unable to locate the child, according to a Democratic lawmaker who described the case as “despicable”.

Video obtained by NBC News shows the boy being led away by three armed officials after he was summoned to what his family said was a routine immigration appointment in San Diego on 4 November.

Continue reading...
title: Haitian boy, 8, detained by ICE is now unaccounted for, lawmaker says

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Conservation group acquires former US president’s family farm with plans to transfer it to the state in 2028

Jimmy Carter’s family farm has been acquired by a group dedicated to permanently protecting the south-west Georgia land where the late former president’s conservation ethic took hold, officials announced on Monday.

A statement from the Conservation Fund said it plans to open Carter’s family farm – on about 2,458 acres (995 hectares) outside his home town of Plains, Georgia – to the public for hunting, fishing and other outdoor recreation as soon as 2027, with the group set to transfer the land to the state’s natural resources department in 2028.
title: Jimmy Carter’s Georgia farm to open to the public: ‘This land shaped him and his legacy’

author: Presented by Nosheen Iqbal with Maeve McClenaghan; produced by Eleanor Biggs and James Tindale; sound design by Eli Block; executive producers Homa Khaleeli, Elizabeth Cassin,Rachel Oldroyd and Phil Maynard
description:
Multiple women allege David Walliams abused his power and position as a celebrity to prey on them for sexual purposes when they were young women, an investigation by the Guardian and ITV News has found. He denies the allegations. Maeve McClenaghan reports

David Walliams, the comedian and former Britain’s Got Talent judge, is alleged to have groomed fans he met when they were as young as 15. Walliams denies any wrongdoing.

In this episode, investigations correspondent Maeve McClenaghan tells Nosheen Iqbal about the investigation by the Guardian and ITV News.

You can watch this podcast on YouTube.

The ITV News documentary David Walliams: Power and Silence is available to watch on YouTub
title: The allegations against David Walliams - podcast

author: Melody Schreiber
description:
Earlier doses for children, a focus on unvaccinated adults, a risk strategy based on geography – here’s how a functioning ACIP would address the measles outbreak

The US has announced three deaths associated with measles last week, among them a seven-month-old baby in New York and a postpartum woman in Pennsylvania, underscoring the need for a more aggressive vaccination approach – but US recommendations haven’t changed.

Dismantling the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) made it harder for the US to respond to the measles outbreak, with vaccine recommendations staying the same during a historic rise in cases and deaths, four former advisers say.

Continue reading...
title: The vaccine limbo in the US is worsening the measles outbreak

author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
description:
Exclusive: Ellen Sandell says Labor’s decision not to back progressives in key inner-seat could hand power to right-wing coalition in close election

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Victorian Greens say Labor’s “frankly unforgivable” decision not to preference the minor party in a key inner-city seat could hand the upcoming election to a Liberal-One Nation coalition.

The party’s leader, Ellen Sandell, lambasted Labor’s decision on Tuesday to run an open ticket in Prahran, an inner Melbourne seat currently held by the Liberals’ Rachel Westaway on a tiny 1.
title: Victorian Labor’s ‘unforgivable’ preferences decision risks Liberal-One Nation government, Greens warn

author: Lauren Aratani in New York
description:
New data comes after Republicans’ midterms losses – which were largely seen as a rebuke of the party over high prices

US inflation rose 0.4% from September to October, slightly above expectations but still a cooldown in price increases as the cost of gas dipped during the month.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics did not release the usual year-over-year inflation figure as part of the consumer price index (CPI), which measures the price of a basket of goods and services, as data was not collected in October 2025 during the government shutdown.

Continue reading...
title: US inflation rose 0.4% in October as price increases cooled and gas costs dipped

author: Joseph Gedeon
description:
Thomas Massie has accused US defense secretary of illegally waging war without congressional authorization and abusing his powers

Pete Hegseth has dismissed a bid to impeach him as a “political spectacle”, accusing the Republican lawmaker who moved to force a vote of trying to stage a “show trial”.

At a press conference on Tuesday, the US defense secretary – accused of illegally waging war without congressional authorization, and abusing his powers – claimed he was simply being pursued by political opponents of Donald Trump.

Continue reading...
title: Hegseth calls Republican’s bid to impeach him a ‘stunt’ by critics of Trump

author: Dara Kerr
description:
California saw the most expensive opposition campaign in its history as funding of political campaigns broke records in the US midterms

In the hours after polls closed on election day, tech industry players began praising Sergey Brin, the co-founder of Google, on social media.

“Huge thanks to Sergey Brin here,” wrote Garry Tan, the CEO of Y Combinator. Venture capitalist Ilya Sukhar posted: “God bless Sergey Brin.” And David Marcus, a crypto entrepreneur, simply wrote: “Hero.”

Continue reading...
title: Tech’s biggest names sunk a tax on billionaires’ wealth with $425m and a familiar playbook

author: Associated Press
description:
If data from device is recovered, it could give crucial details about what pilots said as they lost control of aircraft

Investigators said Monday they have recovered the cockpit voice recorder from a business jet that plummeted from the sky amid severe weather in Florida eight days earlier, killing all nine people on board.

The recorder was found at the site where the Bahamas-bound Learjet slammed into the ground in Palm Beach county, Florida, and erupted in a fireball 1 November, the National Transportation Safety Board said in a statement posted to social media.

Continue reading...
title: Investigators recover voice recorder from Florida jet crash that killed nine people

author: Fiona Harvey in Antalya and Rebecca Bailey
description:
Former US secretary of state says most nations are ‘stumbling along’ while Beijing has ‘hugely accelerated’

  • Cop31 live – latest updates

China is leading the world in moving away from fossil fuels, and the rest of the globe – including the US – must now follow, the former US secretary of state John Kerry has told the Guardian, as Cop watchers wonder exactly how China is going to approach this year’s climate summit.

As Cop31 opens – this year the climate conference is in Turkey – there is plenty of speculation about whether China will finally step into the leadership role that it has long avoided. In its latest “five-year plan” adopted in March 2026, China for the first time pledged to “actively partici
title: US and rest of world must follow China’s lead on green energy, says John Kerry

author: Maeve McClenaghan, Rachael Healy and Rachel Oldroyd
description:
Guardian reports accusations after court rejects legal attempt to prevent publication. Walliams denies any wrongdoing

  • Read the full investigation: ‘It wasn’t long until he asked me if I’d ever had sex before’

  • Explainer: the key legal issues surrounding the case

David Walliams, one of Britain’s best-known television personalities and top-selling children’s authors, has been accused by multiple women of using his power and celebrity status to prey on young women and teenagers for sex.

The allegations include accounts from two women who said they first met the star when they were 15 years old.

Support for anyone affected by sexual abuse issues is available in the UK f
title: Revealed: David Walliams accused of using celebrity status to prey on young women for sex

author: Martin Belam
description:
Speaking in the White House, the president said the US remained ‘locked and loaded’ but escalation was not needed. Plus how Grand Theft Auto became a cultural colossus

Good morning. Oil prices have dropped after Donald Trump unilaterally declared that the US war on Iran was “effectively over”. During a White House press conference, Trump said Israel and Gulf allies in the region were well protected from Iran and that an escalation was not needed.

He said, however, that the US remained “locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason”, adding: “We’re seeing momentum toward the end of this conflict. I think it’s going to be ending fairly soon.” Brent crude has dropped below $90, its lowest level since August.

What is the latest development with Pete Hegseth? A
title: Oil price relief as Trump declares US war on Iran ‘ending fairly soon’ | First Thing

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
Lucy Powell says she thought ‘we’d gone past that sort of culture’, and that she regrets setting up Miliband interview with comedian in 2015

  • Brand sentenced to more than 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assault

Labour’s deputy leader, Lucy Powell, has criticised the “depressing” nature of the cross-examination of Russell Brand’s victims during his trial for rape and sexual assault, saying she believed the courts had “long gone past that sort of culture”.

Powell, now the education secretary, also said she regretted the meeting that the former party leader Ed Miliband had with Brand in 2015, when she was Labour’s campaign chief.

Continue reading...
title: Brand barrister’s cross-examination of victims shocking and depressing, says Labour deputy

author: Luca Ittimani
description:
Department store group kept buying new products and fell months behind in payments to some brands despite discussions with administrators

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

David Jones’s administrators have revealed they reviewed its finances six months ago and discussed restructuring the retailer three months before it fell into administration.

The new timeline raises questions over the department store group’s decision to keep buying new products and fall months behind in payments to some brands before it revealed last Thursday it could not pay its debts.
title: David Jones’s finances were reviewed and restructuring flagged months before it fell into administration

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
Conservative leader launches Welfare That Works policy document

The US military has reportedly evacuated aircraft from a second airbase in ⁠Britain after a threat from Iran, Jamie Grierson and Dan Sabbagh report.

Lucy Powell, the deputy Labour leader and education secretary, was giving interviews on behalf of the government this morning. Asked about the RAF Mildenhall story, she told Sky News:

I can’t comment on those sort of live operations, as you know.

But we’re constantly keeping the security of our bases under review and, as we’ve seen with other cases recently, we take firm and quick action where we need to.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Double amputees run marathons,’ says Badenoch as she proposes £36bn cuts to disability and other benefits – UK politics live

author: Yohannes Lowe
description:
Talks in Abu Dhabi are first substantive negotiations in months focusing on ending the conflict which has raged for more than four years

The US special envoy Steve Witkoff, who is leading the American delegation alongside Jared Kushner - Donald Trump’s son-in-law – has just posted on X with details of their meeting with European and Ukrainian officials ahead of the trilateral talks between the US, Ukraine and Russia.

Witkoff said the meeting helped to coordinate their efforts to end the war and “establish the conditions for a durable peace”, including support for “robust security guarantees” for Kyiv. He said officials from Europe, the US and Ukraine shared the same objectives and all held a commitment to “Euro-Atlantic security”.

Participants emphasized that any future arrangements must respect sovereignty, territorial integrity, independent decision-making, and provide cr
title: US, Russia and Ukraine hold trilateral talks aimed at ending war – Europe live

author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Aakash Hassan in Delhi
description:
Hasina fled to India in 2024 after mass uprising. She faces death penalty upon return

Sheikh Hasina is “confident” she will return to Bangladesh in December, according to exiled members of her party, after the disgraced former prime minister of Bangladesh applied for a fresh passport this week.

Hasina has been living in self-imposed exile since August 2024 when she was toppled from power by a mass uprising against her authoritarian rule. She fled over the border to India, where she has since been allowed to live freely in Delhi.

Continue reading...
title: Disgraced former leader Sheikh Hasina plans return to Bangladesh after two years in exile

author: Patrick Commins Economics editor
description:
Westpac survey results signal growing sense of ‘helplessness’ while Jim Chalmers faces growing pressure to rein in spending

Confidence among mortgaged households has crashed to its lowest level in more than three decades amid a growing sense of “helplessness” about the economy, even as a dramatic shift in financial markets suggests there is now a strong chance of a Reserve Bank rate cut by this time next year.

The latest Westpac survey showed its consumer sentiment index sinking again in November to reach a four-year low, amid deepening pessimism about the near-term prospects for the economy.

Continue reading...
title: Mortgage holders’ confidence crashes to lowest level since 1994 as year that ‘feels like a recession’ looms

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Inquiry recommends police investigate allegations of sexual assault and other abuse at Redeemer Baptist school

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A probe into a private religious school accused of sexual, physical, psychological, spiritual and financial abuse has recommended it be barred from enrolling new students.

Former students and teachers of western Sydney’s Redeemer Baptist school told a NSW parliamentary inquiry about a string of disturbing allegations.

Continue reading...
title: Sydney private school accused of sexual abuse should be banned from enrolling new students, inquiry says

author: Henry Belot
description:
Party disendorses Preston candidate Franco Guardiani after social media posts emerge

One Nation Victoria has disendorsed a candidate whose private social media account described Adolf Hitler as the “GOAT” and claimed that “importing Islam is making pedophilia legal”.

In a now deleted social media post, the party’s candidate for Preston, Franco Guardiani, commented on a social media post on X asking people to: “Describe Hitler in one word? Be brutally honest”.

Continue reading...
title: One Nation dumps Victorian election candidate who praised Adolf Hitler as ‘GOAT’

author: Jonathan Barrett Business editor
description:
Australian carrier announces agreement with Accenture amid ‘unprecedented’ technological disruption, CEO Vanessa Hudson says

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Qantas is preparing to cut 850 local jobs and outsource work offshore under an AI-driven overhaul, marking a growing wave of disruption to the Australian workforce.

The changes represent the third major corporate layoff plan announced in Australia in three weeks, after restructuring moves flagged by the design company Canva and National Australia Bank.

<
title: Qantas to cut 850 Australian jobs and outsource work to India under AI-driven overhaul

author: Associated Press
description:
Chamber voted 73-25 to formally take up bill that will shorten timelines to start energy and datacenter projects

The Senate on Monday advanced bipartisan legislation aimed at speeding up permitting reviews for datacenters and other infrastructure projects, in the first major action since last week’s election that soundly repudiated Donald Trump and congressional Republicans.

The Senate voted 73-25 to formally take up the bill, which senators and the president have pushed as a way to meet growing demand for electricity and other forms of energy that now face years-long delays in getting to the grid.

Continue reading...
title: Senate advances bill to speed up permit reviews for infrastructure projects

author: Kat Wong
description:
Former police officer tells jury he joked about being ‘white girl crazy’ with friends as lawyer questions him over start of relationship with Baird

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Beau Lamarre-Condon has denied being “obsessed” with Jesse Baird from the start of their relationship, telling a court he would have liked the TV presenter even if he was “a garbage cleaner”.

The former police officer is accused of fatally shooting Baird and his new partner, Luke Davies, with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney on 19 February 2024.

In Australia, the crisis support service Lifeline is on 13 11 14. In the UK and Ireland,
title: Beau Lamarre-Condon denies being ‘obsessed’ with Jesse Baird as double murder trial continues

author: Hilary Beaumont
description:
Key environmental groups come out against bipartisan Baaja bill over fears it could spur datacenters and ICE jails

It’s a bill that would make it easier to build big infrastructure projects in America – everything from fossil fuel pipelines to transmission lines that would add more clean energy to the grid. And it would roll back environmental and social protections to achieve this goal. That is why climate advocates are torn over the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs act (Baaja), which was scheduled for an initial procedural Senate vote on Monday.

The Senate voted on Monday to open debate on Baaja in the first of several procedural votes. Senators voted 73 to 25 on the cloture motion, which did not result in the bill being passed, but pushed it another step forward.<
title: Senate advances bill to speed up projects from gas pipelines to clean energy

author: Sally Weale Education correspondent
description:
Almost two-thirds of school leaders polled say new regime is much more intense than previous framework

More than half of headteachers in England who were polled after their schools were inspected under Ofsted’s new regime are considering cutting short their careers as a result of the experience.

In response to the question “Has the inspection affected how long you intend to stay in your role?”, 52% of those who responded said they were thinking of leaving their job sooner than planned.

Continue reading...
title: Headteachers consider leaving jobs earlier than planned after new Ofsted inspection
